networth.note: Sum of the 78 asset ranges on his 2026 candidate report (filed under his legal name, Thomas James Feely; period Jan 1, 2025–May 20, 2026). No liabilities disclosed. Includes an NFL defined-benefit pension and an annuity, each $1M–$5M. Sportico's earlier figure ($15.9M–$65.5M) came from his 2025 report.

trades.note: Candidate report; no transaction schedule. Never on a congressional committee.

note.t: 2026 candidate report: largest holdings are Klein Tools (private S-corp, $5M–$25M; he is a board member; dividends $100K–$1M a year), Gevity Inc. (private health company, angel stake, $1M–$5M), four rental properties held in 'Family 49' LLCs (a Champion, MI property at $1M–$5M, others $500K–$1M each in Michigan and Gilbert, AZ), Palantir stock ($500K–$1M) plus Palantir options ($250K–$500K), Micron ($500K–$1M in an IRA), dozens of other individual stocks, about $70K–$180K in crypto (Bitcoin, Ether, XRP, Dogecoin), and an indexed life policy. Earned income in 2026 through May: Yrefy TV ads $50,000, BetMGM appearance $20,000, Auntie Millie's speaking $20,000, Outlyr golf appearance $10,000. Positions: board member of Klein Tools, Strongwatch and Zah Group; president of the Feely Family Foundation; manager of four Family 49 LLCs. Agreement: NFL pension. No foreign income. Foreign-issuer securities include small OTC positions in five foreign mining companies (tickers ending in F), NIO ADRs, Shopify, and Accenture plc and Iterum plc shares. A 2025 amendment (filed Aug 19, 2026) was not read.

democracy.t: Declined during the 2026 primary to say whether Trump lost the 2020 election; on Aug 26, 2026 he acknowledged that Joe Biden won. No statement on the 2024 results or on fraud claims was found.

research_notes: His House filings are under his legal name, Thomas James Feely (the pipeline stored them under az-01-thomas-feely). He took extensions both years (May 22, 2025; May 18, 2026). The 2025 amendment (doc 10082719) was not read. courts stays 'news'.
